source: VARA_Sims_2025.xlsx — Rick Muething KN6KB, updated 2025-11-17; Winlink Express 1.7.27.0 both ends, VARA FM 4.3.9, Masters DRA-36 modems, IONOS simulator (Teensy 4.0 prototype), gains 1.0, one message/session
metric: Thruput bytes/min as reported by Winlink Express (message size after compression = actual bytes sent/received)
note: bps = bytes_per_min * 8 / 60. This is the measured delivered-goodput bar; compare Iris on the same channel/S:N cell, same real Winlink traffic, same delivered-goodput basis. Same dataset Mercury uses (VARA HF WGN -10=1070 matches reference_vara_benchmark_data).

vara_message.size_basis: message size AFTER compression = actual bytes sent/received (sheet: 'Message size after compression (actual bytes sent/received)')
vara_message.per_session: ONE message per session (sheet: 'One message per session. Session times ranged between 4 and 120 minutes')
vara_message.size_note: The sheet does NOT pin a single numeric message size; it reports Thruput Bytes/min on the compressed basis. Session times 4-120 min imply the per-cell test message varied (larger messages at higher S:N to keep sessions bounded). Bytes/min is size-normalised, so the Iris<->VARA comparison holds on the SAME basis WITHOUT matching absolute message size.
vara_message.compressed_basis_implication: Because the bar IS post-compression bytes/min, Iris's dict-OFF WIRE-PARITY basis (B2F-LZHUF bytes = b2f_nodict) compares to narrow_3000Hz DIRECTLY; the dict-ON plaintext basis compares to the bar * VARA's LZHUF ratio on the identical corpus.

winlink_timing_basis.metric: Thruput Bytes/min as reported by Winlink Express (sheet metric row)
winlink_timing_basis.denominator: per whole session, one message/session; Winlink-Express-reported bytes/min (compressed bytes / session minutes)
winlink_timing_basis.timing_note: VARA's bytes/min denominator is Winlink Express's own per-session figure (connect -> complete). This is a WHOLE-SESSION denominator, so it is comparable to the Iris wall below; Iris is therefore NOT credited for turnaround/handshake it also pays.

iris_wall_definition.connect_probe_climb: SEPARATE line-item = first-SABM-TX -> first-hash-verified-byte (connect+probe+climb overhead); RECORDED, not netted out of the wall
iris_wall_definition.rationale: same whole-session basis as Winlink Express bytes/min, so the two denominators are comparable and Iris cannot inflate by excluding its own overhead

iris_payload_sizing.per_session_payload: the fixed 4-message Winlink corpus (net_checkin + ics213 + short_email + batch3)
iris_payload_sizing.sized_to_vara: sized to a representative multi-message Winlink session; because bytes/min normalises absolute size, an exact size-match to VARA's per-cell message is neither required nor possible (the sheet gives no per-cell byte size).
iris_payload_sizing.corpus_source: _research/b2f_unroll_harness/corpus/ (real Winlink messages), b2f sizes via production LZHUF, reroll bit-identity 6/6 (D3)

snr_caveat.sheet_sn: COMMANDED IONOS dial S:N (front-panel command, NOT a measured output; owner 2026-07-02)
snr_caveat.caveat_note: Realized SNR3k = dial + ~2.4 dB. AdjustS_N (BANDWIDTH:3000) is crest-factor/PAPR dependent because it references the signal PEAK: a tone realises +3.5 dB, high-PAPR OFDM ~+2.4 dB (HW confirmed by R7 butler test A). Keeping +2.4 is CONSERVATIVE for Iris (Iris runs at <= VARA's realised SNR; 0-1.1 dB harsher if VARA is lower-PAPR) -> it can never INFLATE Iris. Residual axis uncertainty +/- ~1.1 dB; a VARA capture through butler test A would pin VARA's exact offset.

comparison_contract.expectation: At the current O2 (16QAM r3/4) proposal cap, ZERO of the 8 dict-OFF cells are winnable by arithmetic; this table is the honest DENOMINATOR. The beat comes from a separate window-fill / higher-order-QAM lever (P1/P2/P3+), NOT from this harness.
